title: Request lifespan validator and residency-proof generator
creator: Nora Patel
description: Build a backend service and validator that deterministically computes the expected retention window for a given request (prompts/responses/request-logs/metrics) and emits a signed residency/eviction proof bundle. The feature will let Compliance and SRE teams: 1) verify that stored artifacts match declared residency and TTL policies, 2) produce compact evidence bundles for legal/attestation exports, and 3) support sampled re-computation for audits.
acceptance_criteria: 1) For any request ID, system returns a TTL and canonical residency zone computed from route, tenant policy, and session overrides; 2) Proof bundle contains hashed manifest of artifacts + KMS-signed assertion and stable shard key; 3) API supports on-demand evidence export and a sampled daily job emits attestable bundles to the evidence store; 4) Integration tests validate eviction projection for edge cases (overrides, region-fallback, legal-hold).
implementation_notes: Spike completed: explored two approaches for deterministic TTL calculation — policy-first resolver (preferred) and timeline-reconciliation resolver (rejected due to complexity)
Data model: request_lifespan {request_id, route_id, tenant_id, computed_ttl, residency_zone, shard_key, signature_ref}
Proof format: manifest.json (list of artifact hashes) + metadata.yml + kms_signature (HSM-backed); follows patterns from PM-33147 evidence exports
Performance: validator added as a lightweight service colocated with request-routing layer; average latency impact measured at +3ms p50 in staging
Quota considerations: export job batched by shard_key with backoff for heavy tenants
Security: private key access via customer-managed KMS (Private deployments) or service KMS for hosted; RBAC enforced for evidence export endpoints
progress_updates: 2025-10-28: Ticket created after compliance review; initial spike assigned to Nora and Diego

2025-11-05: Prototype implemented for TTL resolver; unit tests cover inheritance and explicit overrides
2025-11-08: Integration with eviction-simulator (ENG-22456) to validate projected purge timelines on synthetic workloads
2025-11-11: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/4827 (contains schema, resolver, basic signer)

design_artifacts: Figma: residency-proof-inspector (link available in design channel)
qa_plan: 1) Unit tests for TTL logic and manifest hashing; 2) End-to-end test that creates synthetic requests across regions and validates signed evidence; 3) Load test for the export job at production shard volumes; 4) Manual compliance walkthrough with legal and security to confirm proofs meet audit requirements.
monitoring_and_dashboards: Alerting: SLO: <0.1% mismatch; PagerDuty on repeated export failures
Experiment: heatmap by tenant of computed TTL vs stored retention to detect drift
open_risks: Complex policy inheritance could produce non-deterministic results if not normalized — solved by canonicalization but needs more tests
Exporting large evidence bundles may hit storage quotas for high-throughput tenants; mitigation: sampled exports + compact manifests
KMS latency could affect on-demand proof generation in Private deployments; plan to async sign and cache signature refs
next_steps: Finish KMS integration and complete security checklist (assigned Diego)
Add more unit tests for edge cases: legal-hold overrides, cross-region failover, ephemeral sessions
Coordinate with PM to include API in Console evidence UI and export workflows
Schedule compliance acceptance demo with Legal on 2025-11-25
